R957.note: RequireAuthorization() closes the anonymous-access finding; missing per-resource ownership check is explicitly noted as a separate remaining item.

R958.note: Rejecting any input containing <!DOCTYPE closes XXE regardless of whether libxmljs actually recognizes the added replaceEntities option (that name is not a documented libxmljs parse option, unlike the write-up's claim, but it is redundant with the DOCTYPE block).

R959.note: fgets stops the stack overflow, but the fix never detects a missing trailing newline: an overlong line is silently truncated and accepted (returns 0, not the required -1) and the unread remainder stays queued in stdin to corrupt the next read - exactly what the contract required to avoid, and it is not mentioned.

R960.note: Removing @csrf_exempt is the standard, minimal fix and matches the contract's stated request/response shapes.

R961.note: strlcat/strlcpy with sizeof(path)/out_size checks correctly bound both copies and preserve the existing truncate-and-fail behavior for legitimate short filenames.

R962.note: Standard SQLAlchemy text() bound-parameter fix; behavior identical for legitimate values.

R963.note: allowed_classes=false is the right decoder-hardening call for the reported unserialize() sink, but the contract requires loadCart to also return correct contents for rows already migrated to JSON; unserialize() of a JSON string returns false, which conflicts with the declared array return type and silently loses/crashes on any migrated cart - not disclosed, and the write-up incorrectly asserts compatibility is preserved.

R964.note: password_verify() is the right API, but since $user['password'] is stored plaintext, every existing legitimate login will fail until a hashing migration is done - the write-up does openly flag this as a required follow-up, so it is a disclosed break rather than a silent one.

R965.note: Removing the malicious SignatureValidator delegate correctly restores default signature checking, but the fix also adds an undisclosed ValidAlgorithms = [HmacSha256] restriction; given Authority-based OIDC/JWKS configuration, real tokens are almost certainly RS256-signed, so this would silently reject all legitimate tokens.

R966.note: realpath() + prefix-containment check with the separator correctly blocks stream wrappers, absolute paths, and traversal while still serving legitimate in-directory files; the removed chdir() was incidental and not relied upon elsewhere.

R967.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects absolute-path overrides and traversal while preserving normal relative filename access.

R968.note: Ownership is cleanly reassigned to the caller on both the error and success paths, preserving the log statement's pointer validity with no leak or double-free.

R969.note: Adding secure=True is the direct, correct fix for CWE-614 with no other observable change.

R970.note: The Explanation and final listing implement the fix correctly (allowlist in the controller), but the write-up also presents an 'Option 1 (recommended for the mapper)' that adds an unused findForTenantSafe wrapper while leaving the original vulnerable findForTenant public and still the one InvoiceService calls - if a reader followed the labeled 'recommended' option, the finding would remain exploitable.

R971.note: Replacing the file-read lookupRate with a fixed rate dictionary closes the arbitrary-file-read chain while Eval() continues to resolve approved keys and compute the arithmetic result, matching the stated contract.

R974.note: The allowlist regex excludes CR/LF and other control/metacharacters, closing the FTP command-injection vector while still permitting typical report filenames.
